claim.statement: Albumin increases the solubility of calcium carbonate and phosphate, whereas its breakdown products dissolve them much less; hence skeletal calcium salts are thrown down when proteins are broken down in metabolism, not by direct action of carbonic acid on a more soluble salt.
claim.quote: The probability is, therefore, that the actual precipitation of the calcium salts is not due to the direct action of carbonic acid, etc. on a more soluble salt (as was at one time believed); but to catabolic changes in the proteids of the organism, which tend to throw down the salts already formed, which had remained hitherto in albuminous solution.

why_this_protein: Thompson attributes the solubility of skeletal calcium salts to "albuminous solution" and "the proteids of the organism". Serum albumin is the albumin that carries calcium in blood: UniProt annotates it as the major plasma calcium transporter with annotated Ca(2+) binding sites. This record anchors the claim's named substance to a concrete molecule and its predicted structure.

protein.name: Albumin
protein.uniprot_function_annotation: Binds water, Ca(2+), Na(+), K(+), fatty acids, hormones, bilirubin and drugs. Its main function is the regulation of the colloidal osmotic pressure of blood. Major zinc transporter in plasma, typically binds about 80% of all plasma zinc (By similarity). Major calcium and magnesium transporter in plasma, binds approximately 45% of circulating calcium and magnesium in plasma (Probable). Potentially has more than two calcium-binding sites and might additionally bind calcium in a non-specific manner (PubMed:22677715). The shared binding site between zinc and calcium at residue Asp-272 suggests a crosstalk between zinc and calcium transport in the blood (Probable). The rank order of affinity is zinc > calcium > magnesium (Probable). Binds to the bacterial siderophore enterobactin and inhibits enterobactin-mediated iron uptake of E.coli, and may thereby limit the utilization of iron and growth of enteric bacteria such as E.coli (PubMed:6234017). Does not prevent iron uptake by the bacterial siderophore aerobactin (PubMed:6234017)

what_this_does_and_does_not_show: It shows that a hosted BioNeMo model can be called from this repo on a real, checksummed sequence and that the result can be filed against a claim with provenance (model, endpoint, version, time, input hash).
A predicted structure does not test Thompson's claim about solubility; the claim's status is unchanged by this record.
The next real step would be a pre-registered claim test against solubility measurements, not more structure predictions.
Anything genome-related is out of scope here and would be labelled a sketch.
